summary: identity.toml gained a `pulse` platform (game-server-monitor game presence), matched on a SteamID64 — so the Games Hub web portal can resolve a Pulse player back to the same person_id their Signal/Discord/Life360 accounts already share.
details: nora/domain/identity.py: `pulse` id-kind vocabulary is `steam_id` only — deliberately not Pulse's own `player_key`, which is that one game's EOS Product User ID and does not carry over to a different title, unlike SteamID64.

nora/persons_file.py: `[[persons.<id>.pulse]]` is a 6th platform block, same array-of-accounts shape as signal/discord/life360 — one block per account, `persons.resolve("pulse", steam_id)` works the same way `persons.resolve("life360", member_id)` already does.

Companion change on game-server-monitor's own REST API (mikeng-io/game-server-monitor@669ded6): GET /v1/servers/{id}/players/{playerKey} now echoes steamId, bearer-gated like every other /v1/* route — it was already captured internally to locate save files, just never republished before.
limitations: Nothing in nora/web or the portal UI resolves through this yet — identity.toml carries the mapping, but no route currently calls persons.resolve("pulse", ...) to show a resolved name on a games page.
